_comment: Illustrative figures set for the demonstration, not any company's data. They exist so a scenario can be read in money and days: how much annual spend runs through the suppliers it touches, how long stock lasts (time to survive) and how long qualifying a new source takes (time to recover). Replace with the client's own numbers in a live build.

scenarios.title: Typhoon and port backlog cut Guangdong for three weeks
scenarios.what: Factories in Shenzhen and Huizhou close for several days, then the ports take the rest of three weeks to clear the backlog.

scenarios.title: Rhine low water for a month
scenarios.what: Barges through Kaub sail at a fraction of their load, so goods moving by river via Basel arrive late or move to road and rail at higher cost.

scenarios.title: One acetate tow plant goes down for six weeks
scenarios.what: A fire or long shutdown at one of the four tow producers on the watchlist. Global tow capacity is tight, so the others cannot simply absorb the volume.
